lines.en: I tap on Uta’s name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
It’s still early, so the chances of her being asleep are pretty high. But, then again-

But, then again, with the archery club actually being the only real club at Kumon-mi High and Uta being the ace of it, I wouldn’t be surprised if she was already on her way over there.
Which, by the sound of it, she likely is.

: Plus, you’ve yet to come to my house while no one else is home and I think the time has come.

: What even was that?
: I just spit my friggin’ tea all over my bed, that’s what! You’re inviting me to your house?!
: Yeah.
: While no one else is home?! It would be just the two of us?!
: That is what is happening, yes.
: Do you have any idea how many phone calls I have to make now?! Do you have any idea what you’ve done?!
: Are you coming or not?
: No! No way! That’s the point of no return! I don’t know what kinda crazy morning wood you had to wake up with to propose something like this, but it’s not happening! No way!
: I bet you’d come over if I was that talking sponge you used to have a crush on.
: Stop bringing up the sponge!
: If you’re not going to come over, could you at least meet up with me somewhere?
: Ugh...why are you so pushy today? And why does it have to be when I already have a thing to do?
: Because I know you’ll cave and choose me if I keep pestering you about it.
: Mngh...
: And I want to see you.
: I want to see you too...
: Say that again?
: Aaah! I said meet me at the park! Bye!
Uta hangs up the phone and my first victory of the day comes as soon as I wake up.
I feel a little guilty about making her skip the one [[non-extortionate] thing she’s really good at, but it will all be worth it soon enough.
Because after the bashfulness wears thin and the first few steps in cracking her mask of reluctance have been made, she’ll be something worth treasuring.
She’s that right now, of course. But she can be more.
And I know she wants to be more.
I can feel it when she’s near.
I can see it in her eyes and hear it when she speaks.
And it feeds the evil part of me.
I had a dream last night.
That dream made me wake up hungry.
: There...are you happy now? You got a teenage girl to skip morning practice for you.
: You look nice today.
: Th...Thanks...but...I don’t know if it’s the best idea to say that sort of stuff with all these people around. They might get the wrong idea about us.

: Ah! I knew this was a date! You tricked me into meeting you here by throwing out an idea like coming over to your place because you knew I’d refuse and have to meet you in public instead!
: Uta, I can be a very calculating person at times. That much is inarguable. But you are giving me way too much credit and putting way too much thought into what I’m actually calculating.

: You don’t have to worry about me, Uta. I’m old enough to make my own decisions.
: And I, unfortunately...am not. Not for a few more years at least. Or until I get off my parents’ phone plan.

: But...to...to get back to the date thing...could we maybe, like...not call it that? Because that makes it feel like I’m doing something wrong and...

: Thank you...
: And...and sorry for being weird about this. And...I guess I’ll just apologize in advance for every other meeting we have like this in the future, where I will also be flighty and awkward.

: You can compensate me by joining me over there where there are less people to eavesdrop on us.
: Thanks, Sensei. I- wait a minute! Ain’t it me who’s supposed to be getting compensated?!
: Probably not something you should yell in broad daylight.

: You’re making it worse.
: Yeah, because you abandoned me when I needed you most!
: Hah...
Uta and I retreat to a corner of the park where the passersby are minimal, leaving us to wallow in momentary self-pity and stifled arousal.
And yes, I may have jumped the gun by using her obvious feelings for me as bait in an attempt to reel her in, but things are clearly a little more complicated than that, and...
And I didn’t really think about how this would look from her perspective.
It wasn’t all that long ago where she was opening up about her past to me. And for me to learn all of that and subsequently jump to “You should come over to my place” isn’t really a good look.
It’s an accurate one. That I won’t deny. But it’s not good.
And I can be good now.
: Well, that didn’t go perfectly.
